clue.text: One's back put out — by this exercise?

indicators.note: back tells us to read the letters of one's (as I'S, 'one is') in the reverse direction

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals, so one's is I'S

indicators.note: put out suggests something knocked out of shape, so the letters of put are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gym-goer wonders whether this exercise is what put their back out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS (one's, I'S) into SI; 'out' rearranges PUT into TUP. The surface hint that the exercise wrecked a back makes the whole clue a wry comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-up is a standard abdominal workout move, lying down and raising the torso.

clue.text: Reluctantly agree to lay protective material over gold

parts.note: to lay something is to set it down

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so this word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: felt is used as protective padding, as in roofing felt
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A builder grudgingly accepts laying felt on top of gilding.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle for something is to accept it though it is less than you wanted.

clue.text: Anklebone can be fixed in hospital usually

indicators.note: something fixed in is lodged within, so the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: A broken ankle bone is normally set in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: The talus is the bone at the ankle that connects the leg to the foot.

clue.text: Anti-Euro move?

parts.note: split as for the British currency, a stance against the European coin; also to put forward a proposal

explanation.surface: A political manoeuvre against adopting the single European currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound is to put forward an idea, as one moves a motion.

clue.text: Skiffle instrument enlivened a drab show

indicators.note: enlivened suggests the drab letters being livened up and stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A dull performance gets a lift from a skiffle band's instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enlivened' rearranges the letters of A DRAB SHOW. Skiffle was a 1950s British craze of homemade-instrument folk-jazz bands.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbed laundry board was played with thimbles as a percussion instrument in skiffle groups.

clue.text: Bundles of papers with advertisements

parts.note: ads is short for advertisements

explanation.surface: Stacks of newspapers come stuffed with adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: Wads are thick rolls or bundles, typically of banknotes or paper.

clue.text: Song introduced by former comperes doing a turn: Any Old Iron?

indicators.note: introduced by here means brought in among, so the song is put inside
doing a turn, a variety act, here means turning around so the letters read backwards

parts.note: late means former, as in the late chairman
MCs, masters of ceremonies, are comperes
rap is a style of song

explanation.surface: Old music hall comperes perform a turn introducing the song Any Old Iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing a turn' sounds like a variety act but reverses the pieces, giving SCMETAL. Any Old Iron is a London music-hall song, the cry of a rag-and-bone man buying junk.
explanation.definitionFit: The music-hall song's title is a scrap dealer's cry asking for discarded iron.

clue.text: Take ages to become accepted socially

definitions.meaning: to take a long time, split as two words
to fit in and be accepted as part of a group

explanation.surface: It takes a long time for a newcomer to be welcomed in society.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it means take a long time; as one word it means to fit in a group.

clue.text: Big American stadium, or a modest construction?

indicators.note: a construction is something built, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Either a huge US arena or a humbler building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' rearranges OR A MODEST. The original was Houston's domed stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: The Houston Astrodome was a famous huge covered sports stadium in Texas.

clue.text: Make loaf and cake in the American way

parts.note: to make something is to do it
loaf and nut are both slang for the head

explanation.surface: A baker makes bread and an American-style cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Donut is the US spelling of doughnut, a fried ring cake.

clue.text: Rumour about noble king's unreasonable demand

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the rumour word wraps the noble

parts.note: a rumour is a tale someone tells
a lord is a noble
R, from Rex, is the standard abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Gossip about a lord spreads word of a king's excessive demand.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a request that is very hard or unreasonable to fulfil.

clue.text: Language — beginning to learn at home

indicators.note: beginning to points at the opening letter of the word learn

parts.note: being at home is being in

explanation.surface: Someone starts learning a language without leaving the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The classical tongue of ancient Rome, still taught in schools.

clue.text: Class with fewer commitments?

parts.note: fewer means less
commitments are things you have on, as in 'I have a lot on'

explanation.surface: A student hopes to find a course that makes fewer demands on their time.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone with fewer commitments has LESS ON; read as one word it is a period of teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A school class or period of instruction is a synonym.

clue.text: Extends trips abroad

parts.note: a spin is a short trip, as in a spin in the car
abroad can mean out, outdoors or away from home

explanation.surface: Someone lengthens their holidays overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something out is to prolong it, making it last longer.

clue.text: Making a big profit is daily activity here?

definitions.meaning: making a lot of money, an idiom for a killing
a daily is a British term for a cleaning lady, so her work in the home

explanation.surface: Big profits are made because cleaning goes on every day.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means profiting hugely; literally it is what a daily cleaner does.

clue.text: Redeployed fielders in non-crucial matches

indicators.note: redeployed means positioned afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket captain moves the fielders around because the games don't matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly matches are games played with nothing at stake in any competition.

clue.text: Is priest wicked in city?

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
wicked means bad

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a holy man in town is evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan.

clue.text: With regular departures from Oslo and Cairo, take to the air

indicators.note: regular departures means every other letter leaves, so we keep the second and fourth of each city

explanation.surface: Flights leave regularly from Oslo and Cairo as planes climb skyward.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping alternate letters of OSLO leaves SO, and of CAIRO leaves AR.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise up and fly high in the sky is a synonym.

clue.text: One whose work was AI?

parts.note: AI looks like artificial intelligence but is A1, the main road from London to Edinburgh, so its builder

explanation.surface: A computer scientist who built artificial intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: A road builder; the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, London to Edinburgh.

clue.text: Vamp with long hair has dad losing his head

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair

indicators.note: losing his head means the first letter is dropped from the father word

parts.note: pater is old British slang for father

explanation.surface: A seductive woman with flowing locks makes a father lose his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing his head' removes P from PATER, leaving ATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A vamp is a seductive woman who preys on men, a femme fatale.

clue.text: Official register's function under discussion

indicators.note: something under discussion is being spoken about, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a function is a role

explanation.surface: A committee debates the purpose of an official record.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a list of names, such as an electoral register.

clue.text: My purpose is to film a dramatisation of Isherwood

definitions.meaning: a camera's statement of what it does: its job is filming
John Van Druten's 1951 play adapted Christopher Isherwood's Berlin stories

explanation.surface: A filmmaker declares their aim of adapting Isherwood.
explanation.definitionFit: The play's title is literally what a filming device would say about itself.

clue.text: One woman having argument with another

parts.note: a row is an argument
another woman, Ena, a girl's name

explanation.surface: One woman is quarrelling with another.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowena is a woman's name, famous from Scott's Ivanhoe.

clue.text: American fellow enlisted among spies in distant land

indicators.note: enlisted among means joining the ranks inside, so these pieces go within the spies

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency
bod is British slang for a person or fellow

explanation.surface: An American joins the spy service in a faraway country.
explanation.walkthrough: Bod is British slang for a person; 'enlisted among' signals putting pieces inside, like recruits joining the ranks of the agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a Southeast Asian country, distant from Britain.

clue.text: Go bang

definitions.meaning: a go is an attempt, as in have a go
a bang is a sharp loud noise, a report

explanation.surface: An instruction to explode.
explanation.definitionFit: Have a crack is to have a go; a crack is also a sudden loud report.

clue.text: Borders of hedge not visible, hidden by odd eucalyptus

indicators.note: hidden by means covered or enclosed, so the inner letters go inside

parts.note: odd means rum, strange

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters, which here are to be dropped
not visible tells us those borders vanish, leaving only the inner letters

explanation.surface: A gardener notices a strange eucalyptus hides the edges of the hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is British for strange; 'Borders of' with 'not visible' strips the first and last letters, and 'hidden by' puts what is left inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The red gum is an Australian species of eucalyptus tree.

clue.text: A number of people drink endlessly at university

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off the drink

parts.note: grog is rum and water, or drink generally
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A crowd of students are drinking without end at college.
explanation.definitionFit: A group is a collection or number of people gathered together.

clue.text: Repair final section of motorway

parts.note: M is used for a British motorway, such as the M1
the final section is the end

explanation.surface: Roadworks fix the last stretch of a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something is to repair or fix it.

clue.text: Walk miles in island, going in westerly direction

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west is going right to left, so the letters are read backwards
in places the miles inside the island

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A stroll of some miles across an island, heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside ELBA to give ELBMA; 'going in westerly direction' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace.

clue.text: Volume of visitors

parts.note: volume suggests quantity of people, but read as a book belonging to those who visit, where they sign their names

explanation.surface: A hotel boasts about how many visitors it gets.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitors' book is a volume in which guests write their names and comments.

clue.text: Classic novel had only limited success as children's bedtime story?

definitions.text: Classic novel had only limited success as children's bedtime story?

parts.words: Classic novel had only limited success as children's bedtime story?
parts.note: a Stevenson novel title, read as a child that dozed only briefly, a bedtime that half worked

explanation.surface: A parent laments that reading a classic at bedtime barely sent the children off.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the title as KID NAPPED: the child had a nap, but only a short one.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson's 1886 adventure novel about David Balfour.

clue.text: More mature traveller visiting Ireland in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller

explanation.surface: An older salesman visits Ireland after retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Riper is the comparative of ripe, meaning more fully developed.
